cards.subject: The First Sunday of Advent: on a low stand just outside the altar rail, an evergreen Advent wreath of fir and holly with red berries and a few pine cones, holding four tall candles — three violet and one rose — only the first violet candle lit, its small flame steady. Beyond the rail, a sanctuary of stone and gilt and a high altar with gradines: six tall candlesticks, unlit, on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in violet silk; a violet frontal with gold orphreys; no flowers. Above the altar, a round window shows a deep blue pre-dawn sky over a snowy village with a single bright morning star. No people. Quiet, expectant, nocturnal light. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The Advent wreath as the Directory on Popular Piety describes it (four candles lit Sunday by Sunday, 'the prophetic light gradually illuminating the long night'), with the widespread custom of three violet candles and one rose; violet for Advent (GIRM 346d) and the moderate floral decoration GIRM 305 asks for. The subject is the test draft x_advent_sunday, kept.

cards.subject: An early weekday Low Mass in Advent, before dawn, in a small stone parish church lit only by candles. At the far end, beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a violet Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast; a young server in black cassock and white surplice kneels on the lowest step at the side. It is a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in violet silk; a violet frontal; no flowers. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind or in profile, a few faithful in winter coats kneel in the wooden pews, each holding a small lit candle: an old woman in a dark headscarf, a young father with his daughter in a knitted bonnet, a nun in a grey habit. The tall windows are still deep blue with the first pale light at their base. Hushed, watchful, warm pools of candlelight in the dark. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The ordinary weekday Mass of Advent in violet (GIRM 346d) with moderate decoration (GIRM 305), set before dawn after the collect of the week's Monday, which asks to be found 'watchful in prayer'. The candles in the pews recall the dawn Advent Masses kept in many places; the Mass shown is the weekday's own, not the Marian votive (Rorate) Mass, which would be white.

cards.subject: The Third Sunday of Advent. In the foreground, on a low stand outside the altar rail, the evergreen Advent wreath with three candles lit — two violet and the ROSE one — and one violet candle still unlit. Beyond the rail, in a brighter church of stone and gilt, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a ROSE-coloured, gold-orphreyed, Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast, no higher than his shoulders; two servers in cassock and surplice kneel at either side of the step. It is a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in rose silk; a rose frontal worked in gold; a few small sprays of white flowers stand on the gradine between the candlesticks. Soft rose-gold morning light falls through the windows. Joyful but restrained. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin rose ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and rose; no halo
cards.basis: GIRM 346f allows rose 'where it is the practice' on Gaudete Sunday (the repo's formulary gives the day's colour as violet, the obligatory one); the wreath's rose candle is lit this Sunday by custom. Flowers stay moderate, arranged around the altar (GIRM 305).

cards.subject: A church's Christmas crib at night during a Sunday of Christmas Time. At the side of the nave, outside the altar rail, a wooden stable with a thatched roof on a bed of straw and moss, with painted carved statues (clearly statues, not living people): the Child in the manger on white linen with arms open, Mary kneeling in blue, Joseph standing with a staff, an ox and a donkey, two shepherds with a lamb; a gilded star hangs above the stable roof. Evergreen boughs, red poinsettias and many small candles glow around it. In front, half-length and seen from behind, a young mother in a Sunday coat, her hair covered with a white lace mantilla, kneels at the crib rail holding her small son, who points at the Child. Behind the crib, beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal embroidered in gold. Warm golden light in the dark church, deep blue windows with stars. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin white ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and white; no halo
cards.basis: The Christmas crib set up in churches, which the Directory on Popular Piety commends for Christmastide, shown on a Sunday of the season; white for Christmas Time (GIRM 346a). Carved statues keep the card apart from the living scene of `nativity_christ` and `holy_family`.

cards.subject: A weekday morning Low Mass in Christmas Time, at sunrise. Beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a WHITE, gold-orphreyed, Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his eyes raised to the crucifix and his hands extended before his breast; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. At the left, small, the church's Christmas crib under its gilded star. A handful of faithful in winter clothes kneel in the front pews, half-length, seen from behind, the women with their heads covered. The first golden rays of the rising sun stream through a tall east window over the altar, lighting the whole sanctuary of stone and gilt. Bright, calm, joyful. cards.subject: A Sunday morning in Ordinary Time outside a small white village church with a bell tower, its bell swinging. Families in their Sunday clothes walk up the path to the open wooden doors: a grandfather with a cane and his hat in his hand, a young couple with a baby, two children running ahead, a woman in a lace mantilla carrying a hand missal; they are small, half-length or seen from behind. Through the open doors, small and deep inside, beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines, its six candles lit, and the priest in a GREEN Roman fiddleback chasuble standing at it with his back to the doors. Around the church, green meadows, a few trees and low hills under a clear blue sky with white clouds; bright, peaceful, ordinary daylight. No lettering. Keep the church and everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin green ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and green; no halo
cards.basis: Green is the colour of Ordinary Time (GIRM 346c); the card shows the Sunday itself, the parish gathering for Mass, rather than a moment of the rite, which the parts-of-the-Mass cards paint. The Second Sunday is chosen as the formulary: the First Sunday of the season gives way to the Baptism of the Lord.

cards.subject: An ordinary weekday morning Low Mass in a simple parish church. Beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a plain GREEN Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. Clear, cool morning light through plain windows. Quiet and unhurried. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin green ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and green; no halo

cards.subject: A Sunday sung Mass in Lent in a large stone parish church, stripped and sober. Beyond the altar rail, a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in violet silk; a violet frontal, and the altar BARE OF FLOWERS. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a VIOLET Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands joined, with two servers in cassock and surplice kneeling on the steps at his sides. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a full congregation kneels in the pews, heads bowed: men bareheaded, women in veils and headscarves, children, an old couple. Along the side walls, the small carved Stations of the Cross. Grey-violet morning light through tall windows. Solemn, penitent, still. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: Lent in violet (GIRM 346d), with the altar that GIRM 305 forbids to be decorated with flowers in this season; the collect of the First Sunday gives the season's theme, and its Gospel every year is the temptation in the desert, hence the caption.

cards.subject: A weekday Low Mass in Lent at a side altar in a quiet chapel on a grey early morning. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a plain VIOLET Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, bowing slightly as he prays; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. The small side altar has a low gradine with a wooden crucifix and two lit candles, an altar card at its centre, a violet antependium, and NO FLOWERS. On the whitewashed wall, a carved wooden Station of the Cross (Jesus falls) without lettering. A few faithful kneel half-length in the foreground, seen from behind or in profile: a man in a worn work jacket with his head bowed, an elderly woman with a black lace veil and a rosary, a young woman in a dark headscarf with joined hands. Cold, soft light from a single high window; bare and sober, but peaceful. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The weekday Mass of Lent in violet (GIRM 346d) with the flowerless altar of GIRM 305; the Stations of the Cross, a devotion the Directory on Popular Piety ties to Lent, are painted as part of the chapel's walls, not as a service.

cards.subject: The Fourth Sunday of Lent: a stone parish church in which, for this one Sunday, the Lenten sobriety lifts a little. Beyond the altar rail, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a ROSE-coloured, gold-orphreyed, Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, his hands extended before his breast, no higher than his shoulders; two servers kneel at the steps. It is a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in rose silk; a rose frontal with gold; for the first time in Lent, two vases of pale spring blossom (almond and white lilies) stand on the gradine between the candlesticks. In the organ loft at the side, small, an organist at the pipes. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a congregation in the pews, the women's heads covered, a child looking up at the flowers. Clear spring light, pale rose and gold, through tall windows. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin rose ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and rose; no halo
cards.basis: GIRM 346f allows rose on Laetare Sunday where it is the practice (the repo's formulary gives violet, the obligatory colour); GIRM 305 and 313 make Laetare the Lenten exception for flowers at the altar and for the organ played alone, which the card paints.
